heroHeadline: China AGI-797 ELINT Ship Confirmed in WPS During Balikatan; Reed Bank Standoff Day 9 Persists; CSIS AMTI: Antelope Reef Now Potentially Largest Island in South China Sea (1,490 Acres, 9,000-Ft Airstrip Footprint) — Three-Front SCS Pressure Unresolved
heroSubtitle: Post-exercise intelligence analysis (May 14-15, 2026) confirmed China's PLA Navy deployed a Type 815A AGI-797 electronic intelligence ship into the West Philippine Sea during Balikatan 2026 (April 20 – May 8, 2026) to collect SIGINT on the allied exercise force of 17,000 troops across 7 nations — the most direct Chinese electronic intelligence effort against any Philippine exercise to date, running in parallel with PLA Task Group 107 live-fire drills east of Luzon (April 24-25), Liaoning carrier Taiwan Strait transit (April 20), and CCG Chuanshan Scarborough training (May 9). The Reed Bank standoff enters Day 9 on May 15 as China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 maintains survey operations near Iroquois Reef within the Philippine EEZ; Beijing has offered no public response to Manila's UNCLOS Article 246 note verbale (filed May 11, five days of diplomatic silence). At Scarborough Shoal, China's 'marine nature reserve' designation remains formally unresolved, the April floating barrier remains in place, and the post-Balikatan AFP monitoring report documented 8 PLAN warships and 9 CCG cutters — the highest single-period Chinese concentration at Scarborough in official records. CSIS AMTI confirmed by May 15 that Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands has reached approximately 1,490 acres — potentially making it the largest island in the South China Sea — with a northwestern edge configured for a future 9,000-ft airstrip, representing China's most significant artificial island construction since the 2013-2016 Spratly campaign; acceleration coincided with a ~30% drop in US SCS reconnaissance flights as carrier groups redeployed to the Middle East. Three concurrent South China Sea confrontations — Reed Bank research vessel standoff (Day 9), Scarborough Shoal marine nature reserve/floating barrier, and Second Thomas Shoal BRP Sierra Madre garrison — collectively represent the most sustained multi-domain Chinese pressure on the Philippines since the West Philippine Sea crisis began, testing diplomatic, legal, and military responses simultaneously. No kinetic Chinese actions against Philippine forces were reported on May 14-15.
